label: input token i in the original phase at position >= 3
explanation: Token detector for the letter i while the original sequence is being read. Fires only when in_tok is i (100% of activation mass) and almost entirely in the original phase. It is silent at t=0-1, weak and rare at t=2 (0.3% of mass), and fires reliably from t>=3 (about 97% of i inputs there). Magnitude is larger for later positions: top examples are i at t=5-6, and the lowest-quartile examples are i at t=2-3. Repeated i (not the first occurrence) fires less often. It does not fire on any other token, on the delimiter, or on i fed back in the copy phase (only 201 weak copy-phase activations). The remaining false positives are scattered i inputs at t>=3 that stay at zero.

issues: The core label holds. On the test split the predicate scores P 0.957, R 0.971, F1 0.964 and mass recall 0.996. The profile confirms that 100% of activation mass is on i inputs, there are 0 activations at t=0-1 or on <DEL>, and the copy phase has only 201 activations with 0.000 mass share.

False claim in the explanation: 'A repeated i (not its first occurrence) fires less often.' Scores show the opposite. With base & (in_first==0), precision is 0.981. With base & (in_first==1), precision is 0.956. Repeated i at t>=3 fires slightly MORE reliably than a first i. The low in_first=0 rate in the profile is pooled over all tokens and does not apply to i.

The false positives are systematic, not 'scattered'. They depend on the first original token, and mostly at t=3. With base & (t==3) & orig(0)==X, precision is: p 0.13, k 0.44, a 0.49, m 0.51, 1 0.63, j 0.88, s 0.86, y 0.86. For most other first tokens it is 1.0 (c d g i l n o q u v w 2 x e h 0 3). A first token of p still suppresses at t>=4 (precision 0.77). Per-t precision is t=3 0.89, t=4-6 >0.99, t=7 0.97, t=8 0.91. The FPs are concentrated at t=3 and, to a lesser degree, at t=8.
The top-activating examples are dominated by sequences that start with x or e. So magnitude also depends on the first token, which the explanation does not mention.

Excluding the first-token class barely changes the score. The predicate base & ~((t==3) & orig(0) in {p,a,k,m,1}) gets test P 0.984, R 0.950, F1 0.967, against 0.964 for the original. The gap is real but carries little mass, so the label is still essentially correct. The explanation needs fixing: drop the repeated-i claim and note that whether the feature fires at t=3 depends on the first token.
